deviation_mechanism: MgF2 (refractive index ~1.43) and Al2O3 (~1.63) provide a low refractive index contrast (Δn ≈ 0.20). Reduced index contrast diminishes the phase shift accumulated per bilayer, forcing the optimizer to rely on increased physical layer thicknesses to maintain the target optical thickness and passband shape. This physical limitation manifests as flattened dispersion gradients, which naturally caps peak reflectivity scores compared to high-contrast stacks (e.g., TiO2/SiO2). The optimizer compensates by expanding specific layers (e.g., shifting away from strict quarter-wave spacings) to broaden bandwidth, trading sharp edge definition for overall transmission efficiency.
